Анкара, 30 қазан 2026 жыл. 30 қазанда Анкарада Түркі мемлекеттері ұйымының (ТМҰ) 13-саммиті өтті. Жиында Қазақстан президенті Қасым-Жомарт Тоқаев Ресейді ұйымға тартуды ұсынды. Саммитке бұл жолы Әзербайжан басшысы қатыспады. Жұма күні Анкарада Түркі мемлекеттері ұйымының саммитін ашқан Түркия басшысы Режеп Ердоған түркі мемлекеттерінің ортақ тарихы мен мәдени мұрасы болашақтағы ынтымақтастықтың негізі екенін айтты. Оның сөзінше, түркі әлемінде алауыздық пен бөлінуге орын болмауы керек. Түркия ұйымға төрағалық ету кезеңінде ортақ тіл, мәдени және спорттық байланыстарды дамытуға, цифрлық сауда мен киберқауіпсіздік саласындағы ынтымақтастықты күшейтуге басымдық береді деді ол. Бүгін ұйым төрағалығы Әзербайжаннан Түркияға өтті. "Түркі әлемінің отбасылық суретінде бөлінуге, жіктелуге немесе алауыздыққа орын жоқ. Біз – біртұтаспыз, бірге тұрмыз және, Алла қаласа, мәңгі бауыр болып қала береміз" деді ол. Түркі мемлекеттері ұйымының саммитінде отырған Түркия басшысы Режеп Ердоған. Анкара, 30 қазан 2026 жыл. ТОҚАЕВ РЕСЕЙДІ ТҮРКІ МЕМЛЕКЕТТЕРІ ҰЙЫМЫНА ШАҚЫРУДЫ ҰСЫНДЫ Саммитте сөз сөйлеген Қазақстан басшысы Қасым-Жомарт Тоқев Ресейді осы форматқа қосылуға шақыруды ұсынды. Бұл жөнінде Ақорда хабарлады. Оның пікірінше, Ресейді "осы форматқа қосылуға немесе ұйымға бақылаушы ретінде қатысуға шақырса, дұрыс әрі әділетті шешім болады". "Өйткені Ресей ірі мемлекет ретінде көне заманнан бері түркі әлемімен тығыз байланыста болған. Бұл елде тарихи мекенін тапқан түркі халықтары көп. Қазіргі таңда Ресей "Алтай өңірі – Түркі өркениетінің алтын бесігі" деген тұжырымдаманы дәріптеуде. Қазақстан бұл тұжырымдаманы қолдайды. Орыс тілінде түркі тілдерінен тамыр тартатын сөздер де аз емес. Жалпы, Ресей түркі елдерінің, яғни біздің Ұйымның бір бөлігі болса, бәрімізге пайдасын тигізер еді” деді Тоқаев. Түркі мемлекеттері ұйымының саммитінде сөз сөйлеп отырған Қазақстан басшысы Қасым-Жомарт Тоқаев. Анкара, 30 қазан 2026 жыл. Ресейді аталған ұйымға шақыру қажеттігі ара-тұра ресейлік сарапшылардан да естіліп қалады. Атап айтқанда, МГИМО халықаралық зерттеулер институтының ғылыми қызметкері Александр Князев 2023 жылы: "Бұл ұйымның жұмысына қатысу оған қатысты көптеген күдікті сейілтіп, Ресей мен Иранның саяси орталарындағы негізсіз алаңдаушылықты азайтар еді" деген еді. Оның сөзінен кремльшіл "Спутник" үзінді келтірген. Ол ұйымға түркі халықтары тұратын Ресей, Қытай, Иранды да қосуға болатынын айтқан. Алғашқы қадам ретінде түркі халықтарының тарихына арналған ортақ оқулық шығаруға болатынын айтқан. Саммит кезінде ұйымның өзге елдермен әріптестігі туралы Өзбекстан басшысы Шавкат Мирзияев та айтқан. Ол түркі мемлекеттері арасында 100 стратегиялық инвестициялық және өнеркәсіптік жобаны іске қосуды ұсынды. Одан бөлек, үшінші елдермен ынтымақтастықты "ТМҰ+" форматы аясында дамытып, сауда, көлік, инвестиция салаларында нақты жобаларды жүзеге асыруға шақырды. "ӘСКЕРИ ОДАҚҚА АЙНАЛМАУЫ КЕРЕК" Ақорданың хабарлауынша, саммит кезінде Тоқаев ұйымның институционалдық құрылымын нығайту қажеттігін де атап өтті. Оның айтуынша, соңғы жылдары ТМҰ қызметі 60 түрлі бағытты қамтитындай кеңейген. Алайда кейбір міндеттер мен функциялар "бірін-бірі қайталайды". Сондықтан ұйымның негізгі жұмыс бағыттары мен басымдықтарын жүйелеу қажет. Ол ТМҰ әскери одаққа айналмауы керек дегенді тағы айтқан. "Осы жылдың мамыр айында Түркістанда өткен жоғары деңгейдегі кездесуде Түркі мемлекеттері ұйымы әскери одақ емес және болашақта да оған айналмауы керек деп мәлімдедім. Бұл – Қазақстанның ұстанымы", – деді Тоқаев. Оның сөзінше, ТМҰ-ға мүше мемлекеттермен тауар айналымы 10 миллиард долларға жуықтаған. Бұл былтырмен салыстырғанда 40 пайызға көп. Осы өсімді сақтау үшін Тоқаев "Түркі әлемінің келешегі – 2040" бағдарламасын жүзеге асыруды және 2027–2031 жылдарға арналған ұйым стратегиясын қабылдауды жеделдетуді ұсынды. Ол Түркі инвестициялық қорының мүмкіндіктерін толық пайдалануға, сондай-ақ Түркі сауда-өнеркәсіп палатасының жұмысын жандандыруға шақырды. "Түркі әлемін өзара байланыстыру ісінде Транскаспий халықаралық көлік бағытының алатын орны ерекше . Биылғы 9 айда Орта дәліз арқылы тасымалданған жүктің көлемі 30 пайызға артты. Соның ішінде транзиттік тасымал көлемі 90 пайызға өсті. Ал Қазақстанның Түркі мемлекеттері ұйымына мүше елдермен теміржол арқылы жүк тасымалы 10 пайызға ұлғайып, 40 миллион тоннаға жақындады. Автокөлікпен тасымалданған жүк көлемі де 20 пайызға көбейіп, 6,5 миллион тоннаға жетті. Осы орайда, біз Қазақстанның транзиттік әлеуетін арттыра түсу үшін елімізде басымдық ретінде арнайы бағдарламаны жүзеге асыратын болдық" деді Тоқаев. Саммите Қырғызстан басшысы Садыр Жапаров Түркияның саяси, экономикалық, әскери және технологиялық салалардағы жетістіктерін атап өтіп, елдің халықаралық беделі артқанын айтты. Қырғызстан басшысы Садыр Жапаров. Түркіменстан басшысы Сердар Бердімұхамедов түркі халықтарының ортақ тарихы мен мәдени мұрасын сақтау және оны келер ұрпаққа жеткізу баршаға ортақ міндет екенін айтты. Ол ұйымды өзара сенімді нығайтып, практикалық ынтымақтастықты кеңейтуге мүмкіндік беретін маңызды алаң деп атады. Сондай-ақ энергетика, көлік, байланыс, өнеркәсіп, ауыл шаруашылығы салаларындағы әріптестікті дамытып, бірлескен инвестициялық және өндірістік жобаларды көбейтуге шақырды. Түркі мемлекеттері ұйымы 13-ші саммитінің қорытындысы бойынша Анкара декларациясы қабылданды. ТРАМПТЫҢ ЕРДОҒАНҒА ХАБАРЛАСУЫ Түркия президент әкімшілігінің коммуникациялар басқармасының хабарлауынша, 29 қазанда Түркия басшысы Режеп Ердоған Түркі мемлекеттері ұйымына мүше елдердің басшыларымен салтанатты кеште отырғанда АҚШ басшысы Дональд Трамп Ердоғанға хабарласқан. Ердоған оған саммитке қатысатын елдердің басшыларының атынан сәлем жолдаған. Anadolu-ның жазуынша, Ердоған Трампқа Анкарадағы Түркі мемлекеттері ұйымының 13-саммитінде ұйымды одан әрі дамытуға бағытталған шешімдер қабылданатынын, 200 миллионнан астам халқы бар ұйым бүгінде Орталық Азиядағы тұрақтылық пен қауіпсіздіктің тірегіне айналғанын айтқан. Ал АҚШ басшысы Дональд Трамп Режеп Ердоғанға Түркі мемлекеттері ұйымының саммитін сәтті өткізуде табыс тілеген. ӘЛИЕВТІҢ САММИТКЕ КЕЛМЕУІ Бұл жолғы саммитке Әзербайжан басшысы Илхам Әлиев келген жоқ. Report агенттігінің хабарлауынша, бұған оның "алдын ала жоспарланған іс-шаралары" мен "жұмыс кестесінің тығыздығы" себеп болған. Саммитке Әзербайжан атынан сыртқы істер министрі Жейхун Байрамов қатысты. Әлиевтің саммитке қатыспайтыны туралы хабар Анкара мен Баку арасында Әзербайжан мектептерінде хиджаб киюге қойылған шектеуге байланысты ашық дау туындағаннан шақта шығып отыр. Түркия президентінің кеңесшісі Октай Сарал Әзербайжанды бұл шектеуді қайта қарауға шақырған. Ал Әзербайжандағы билік партиясы оның мәлімдемесін "жауапсыздық" деп атап, мұндай сөздер екі елдің қарым-қатынасына нұқсан келтіруі мүмкін екенін ескерткен. Дау қыркүйек айында мектеп формасына қатысты ережелер өзгергеннен кейін басталған. Құжатта хиджабқа тікелей тыйым салынбағанымен, кейбір мектептер орамал таққан оқушыларды сабаққа кіргізбей қойған. Бұл жағдай жаппай наразылыққа ұласты. Әзербайжан ішкі істер министрлігі наразылық кезінде 37 адамның ұсталғанын хабарлады. 2009 жылғы 3 қазанда Түркітілдес мемлекеттердің ынтымақтастық кеңесі немесе Түркі кеңесі деген атаумен құрылған ұйым атауы 2021 жылы Стамбұлда өткен саммитте Түркі мемлекеттері ұйымы болып өзгертілді. Сарапшылар оны құрылымның институционалдық және саяси ықпалын кеңейтуге бағытталған өзгеріс ретінде бағалайды. Қазір ұйымға түркітілдес бес мемлекет - Әзербайжан, Қазақстан, Қырғызстан, Өзбекстан және Түркия мүше.

https://daryo.uz/en/2026/10/31/uzbekista.body: Uzbekistan Uzbekistan Railways to introduce additional freight charges for shipments to Afghanistan Uzbekistan Railways will introduce additional freight charges of UZS 800,000–1.3mn ($67–$109) per railcar for most goods transported to Afghanistan from November 7, 2026, excluding wheat, vegetable oil, petroleum products and gas, as the two countries continue discussions on expanding agricultural and economic cooperation. Today, 12:04 2 min read 1 155 views 0 comments 0 Source: “Daryo” / Farrux Aliyev Uzbekistan Railways (O‘zbekiston temir yo‘llari) has announced additional charges for railway freight transportation to Afghanistan, effective November 7, 2026, according to TOLOnews. The additional fees will range from UZS 800,000 to UZS 1.3mn (approximately $67–$109) per railcar, depending on the tariff category. Uzbekistan Railways informs that, the decision was made to prevent a decline in the company's revenue. The new charges will apply to most goods transported through Uzbekistan to Afghanistan. However, wheat, vegetable oil, petroleum products and gas will be exempt from the additional fees. The charges will vary depending on the tariff category and are scheduled to take effect on November 7, 2026. Afghan entrepreneur Omid Haydari stated that higher railway freight transportation costs could affect prices in Afghanistan's domestic market. "Rising costs for rail freight transport could lead to higher prices for goods in Afghan markets. Given that Uzbekistan is cooperating with the people and government of Afghanistan across various sectors, we suggest that they consider reducing transport and transit fees instead," Haydari said. Afghanistan's Deputy Minister of Agriculture, Irrigation and Livestock held an online meeting with Uzbekistan's Deputy Minister of Agriculture to discuss expanding bilateral cooperation in agriculture and livestock. The discussions covered the export of Afghan meat and potatoes to Uzbekistan, development of the cotton and horticulture sectors, and establishment of a seed production center. Sher Mohammad Hatami, a spokesperson for Afghanistan's Ministry of Agriculture, Irrigation and Livestock, stated that the meeting focused on strengthening agricultural and livestock relations between the two countries. "The meeting was held with the aim of strengthening agricultural and livestock ties between Afghanistan and Uzbekistan, as well as fostering trade cooperation, joint investments, and the exchange of technical expertise," Hatami said. According to TOLOnews, Afghanistan's dependence on imports and the costs associated with transporting goods from neighboring countries make economic cooperation with Central Asian states important. The report also noted the need to increase domestic investment and local production in Afghanistan. Economic analyst Abdul Nasir Reshtiya stated that expanding economic relations with Central Asian countries could help Afghanistan diversify its trade routes. "The more Afghanistan expands its ties with Central Asian countries, the greater the opportunities to diversify its trade routes. This, in turn, allows the country to reduce its dependence on a single route," Reshtiya said. # Agricultural Sector Development # Consumer Price Index Impact # Cross-border Logistics # International Economic Policy # Regional Trade Corridors # Uzbekistan-Afghanistan Diplomatic Engagement Reporter Xadicha Abdurashidova All stories Telegram channel @daryo_eng Subscribe What do you think? https://kz.kursiv.media/en/2026-10-30/en.body: Photo: Akorda, photo editor: Dastan Shanay President of Kazakhstan Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has proposed that Russia join the Organization of Turkic States (OTS). He made the statement at the 13th OTS summit in Ankara. According to Tokayev, inviting Russia to cooperate with the organization would be a reasonable and fair step that could also strengthen its international standing. Read also: No ‘Turkic NATO’: Tokayev opposes a military alliance for the OTS . OTS leaders in Ankara / Photo: Akorda «As a major power, Russia has maintained close ties with the Turkic world for centuries. Many Turkic peoples have historically lived within its territory. Furthermore, a significant number of words in the Russian language are of Turkic origin,» Tokayev noted. In his address, Tokayev described the OTS as a unique organization that strengthens the unity of the Turkic world. He emphasized that respect for the sovereignty and national interests of its member states was a fundamental and inviolable principle. Turkic-speaking alliance The OTS, formerly known as the Turkic Council or the Cooperation Council of Turkic-Speaking States, is an intergovernmental organization comprising five member states: Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Turkey and Uzbekistan. Hungary, Turkmenistan and the Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus hold observer status. The organization’s primary goal is to promote comprehensive cooperation among Turkic peoples. The idea was first proposed by Kazakh President Nursultan Nazarbayev in 2006. The organization was established on Oct. 3, 2009, in Nakhchivan, Azerbaijan. Its Secretariat is headquartered in Istanbul. https://www.azernews.az/nation/266529.ht.body: Azerbaijan choosing trade over war in South Caucasus, Hajiyev tells Jeffrey Sachs [VIDEO] 30 October 2026 16:00 (UTC+04:00) Akbar Novruz Read more Azerbaijan is seeking to transform the South Caucasus from a region of geopolitical confrontation into a platform for economic cooperation, regional connectivity and lasting peace, Hikmet Hajiyev, Assistant to the President of Azerbaijan and Head of the Foreign Policy Affairs Department of the Presidential Administration, has said. You can watch the full video down below. Hajiyev made the remarks during a conversation in Baku with American economist and professor Jeffrey Sachs, footage of which he shared on his official X account. Azerbaijan has transformed South Caucasus from “The Battle Space” of big powers to “A Marketplace” or “Cooperation Space”of every party. “In Baku, Professor Jeffrey Sachs sit down with Hikmat Hajiyev, Assistant to the President of the Republic of Azerbaijan, Head of the Department of Foreign Policy Affairs of the Presidential Administration of the Republic of Azerbaijan. From a country that spent 34 of its 35 years of independence at war, to one now quietly building a green corridor from the Caspian Sea to Europe, Azerbaijan is rewriting its own story. Hajiyev reflects on the peace with Armenia, the 800 gigawatts of wind potential sleeping beneath the Caspian, COP29, and a surname that carries within it both an Arabic pilgrimage and a Russian suffix, a dialogue of civilisation in a single word. Professor Sachs delivers the Pope’s encyclical on peace and AI. And somewhere between the caviar and the wind farms, a new picture of the world begins to take shape,” the post stated. In his interview, he stated. "We want to transform the region from a 'battlefield for great powers' into a 'marketplace for great powers.' We have shown our partners that trade is far better than war." He explained that Azerbaijan's approach draws on its experience of attracting international investment into the energy sector, particularly through the 1994 Contract of the Century. "A prime example is the 1994 'Contract of the Century' for the development of Azerbaijan's hydrocarbon resources, for which we invited companies from the United States, Europe, Türkiye, the Arab world, and even Iran," he noted. Green energy corridors and European cooperation Hajiyev also highlighted Azerbaijan's expanding energy partnership with the European Union, noting that cooperation is increasingly extending beyond traditional oil and gas supplies. Referring to a recent visit by European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen, he said discussions had focused not only on hydrocarbons but also on developing a green energy corridor connecting the Caspian region with Europe's electricity network. "Naturally, in previous visits, hydrocarbons and the European market were the dominant factors on our agenda—and they remain so today; that is an unavoidable reality. At the same time, however, a significant portion of our discussions focused on a 'green corridor' stretching from the shores of the Caspian Sea to Europe's energy grid." According to Hajiyev, Azerbaijan expects a substantial increase in renewable electricity generation capacity in the coming years, creating additional opportunities for energy exports. "Azerbaijan possesses immense potential: within just a few years, we will have an additional 2 GW of renewable energy capacity, followed by another 8 GW a couple of years later—all available for export." He linked these ambitions directly to the ongoing peace process with Armenia, arguing that energy connectivity could help demonstrate the economic advantages of regional cooperation. "We are no longer constructing dividing lines or walls; instead, we are building peace and overcoming the fragmentation of our region. We aim to demonstrate the economic benefits of a peace-oriented vision—the 'dividends of peace.' I hope that green energy will become an integral part of this strategy." Azerbaijan chooses lasting peace with Armenia Addressing the history of the Azerbaijan-Armenia conflict, Hajiyev stressed that Baku had chosen reconciliation and economic integration over continued confrontation. He described the peace initiative as a significant political decision following decades of conflict and occupation. "The President and the leadership of Azerbaijan have demonstrated immense political and diplomatic courage, and we have extended a hand of peace to our neighbor, Armenia. We faced two paths: perpetual war or perpetual peace. We chose the path of perpetual peace." Hajiyev emphasised that the objective was not simply to establish a formal diplomatic agreement, but to create practical conditions in which citizens and businesses could experience the benefits of peaceful relations. "This is not merely a declarative peace on paper. We are building a functional, tangible peace—one that people can truly experience, allowing them to appreciate the value of a peaceful life after 35 years of independence, most of which were defined by war." He added that Azerbaijan intended to consolidate these gains through a regional security framework capable of withstanding future challenges. "Now that we are living in peace, we are discovering its true worth; we will cherish it, strengthen it, and use it as a foundation to construct a unique security architecture, one capable of withstanding any negative challenges and ensuring a long-lasting impact for future generations." Tags: Jeffrey D. Sachs Hikmet Hajiyev Azerbaijan-Armenia relations

Uzbekistan and China State Construction Engineering Corporation International (CSCEC International) have discussed opportunities to expand cooperation in construction, urban development and infrastructure projects, including the use of Chinese engineering expertise and technology in Uzbekistan in Tashkent on Saturday. According yo the Uzbekistan’s Ministry of Construction and Housing and Communal Services, the issues were discussed during a meeting between Uzbekistan’s Minister of Construction and Housing and Communal Services Sherzod Khidoyatov and a Chinese delegation led by CSCEC International Chairman Gao Bo. During the meeting, Khidoyatov highlighted Uzbekistan’s efforts to modernize its construction and urban development sectors, upgrade infrastructure and introduce international best practices. He emphasized the importance of expanding cooperation with leading Chinese companies in these areas. The sides exchanged views on developing bilateral cooperation and implementing new projects in areas of mutual interest. Gao Bo noted the company’s participation in various infrastructure projects in Uzbekistan and expressed interest in pursuing additional initiatives based on modern technologies and advanced engineering solutions. Additionally, the discussions covered opportunities to exchange expertise in architecture and engineering, train young specialists and improve the professional qualifications of workers in the construction industry. Both sides emphasized the importance of expanding mutually beneficial cooperation, jointly implementing promising projects and strengthening professional training partnerships. CSCEC International is the international business arm of China State Construction Engineering Corporation (CSCEC), one of China’s largest state-owned construction and engineering groups. The company operates internationally in areas including infrastructure development, building construction, engineering and urban development. https://www.trend.az/casia/tajikistan/42.body: Home Central Asia Tajikistan Tajikistan, China advance 90-km Murghab-Kulma road reconstruction project Tajikistan News 31 October 2026 14:33 (UTC +04:00) Photo: Press Service of the President of Tajikistan Khayal Khatamzadeh Journalist Read more BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 31. Tajikistan’s Ministry of Transport and the Chinese Embassy in the country have signed a protocol on the feasibility study for reconstructing the 90-kilometer Murghab–Kulma highway, the ministry said on October 29. According to the ministry, the document was signed by Transport Minister Azim Ibrohim and Song He, Economic and Commercial Counselor at the Chinese Embassy in Tajikistan. The protocol is based on the findings of research and the feasibility study for the road reconstruction project. It regulates the technical, economic, organizational, and legal aspects of the project, as well as the construction methods and standards to be applied. The 90-kilometer road is being reconstructed with grant assistance from China. Construction is expected to start in 2027. The Kulma Pass, at an altitude of 4,365 meters above sea level, is an important transport link between Tajikistan and China. The crossing supports regional connectivity and trade, and customs and other relevant services operate there. In the first three months of 2026, more than 1,500 trucks and over 3,300 passenger cars entered Tajikistan through the Kulma Pass, along with buses, machinery, equipment, and materials for building industrial facilities. These figures were significantly higher than in the same period of 2025. The flow of tourists through the crossing has also been growing. https://english.news.cn/20261031/71c68a4.body: China Focus: Xinjiang cotton outsmarts extreme heat, external pressure via greater resilience-Xinhua China Focus: Xinjiang cotton outsmarts extreme heat, external pressure via greater resilience Source: Xinhua Editor: huaxia 2026-10-31 16:50:00 URUMQI, Oct. 31 (Xinhua) -- In a 66.7-hectare demonstration cotton field in Changji, northwest China's Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region, the average seed cotton yield reached a record high of 9 tonnes per hectare this year. This would be a strong harvest in any year. It is even more striking as Xinjiang just experienced the hottest summer since 1961. In northern Xinjiang, cotton fields endured 26 days of sustained high temperatures during the critical flowering and boll-setting stage, conditions that would normally cause a plunge in output. Statistics from the China Cotton Association (CCA) put China's cotton planting area in 2026 at 43.054 million mu (about 2.87 million hectares), down 3.9 percent, with an estimated yield of 166.2 kilograms per mu, up 0.5 percent. Meanwhile, Xinjiang's cotton yield is expected to reach 173.8 kilograms per mu, higher than the national average. The region's total output is estimated to account for 95.9 percent of the national total, further consolidating Xinjiang's role as the "ballast" of China's cotton production. How has the Xinjiang cotton industry maintained stable, high output despite the combined pressure of extreme weather, persistent "forced labor" disinformation and external sanctions? Xinhua reporters recently visited cotton fields, factory floors and an industry forum to explore what makes the local cotton industry so resilient. SMART COTTON FIELDS Song Meizhen, chief scientist of the high-quality cotton team at the western agricultural research center of the Chinese Academy of Agricultural Sciences, said the prolonged heat during this year's flowering and boll-setting stage created enormous stress. However, on-site yield measurement by an expert group showed the demonstration field surpassed 600 kilograms per mu, thanks to an integrated technology model combining good seeds, appropriate methods and suitable machinery. The demonstration field is part of a smart cotton field jointly built by the Changji National Agricultural High-tech Industry Demonstration Zone and the research center, where weather stations, soil moisture sensors, inspection robots and drones form an integrated air-space-ground monitoring network. The cotton varieties selected were high-quality, high-yield and multi-resistant lines such as Zhongmian 113. Sensors, notably, collected field data around the clock to enable precise water and fertilizer regulation. Especially in June, July and August, when temperatures exceeded 35 degrees Celsius for nearly 30 days, the intelligent water-fertilizer integrated control system switched irrigation to low-volume, high-frequency water supply, reducing bud and boll shedding caused by heat and drought, Song said. The flowering and boll-setting stage is critical for yield formation: high temperatures can disrupt pollination and cause shedding. In this smart cotton field, however, experience-based farming has been turned into data-based farming, allowing more timely and targeted responses to mitigate possible negative impacts. This year, building on a green and intelligent cotton cultivation system developed over the past two years, the field further integrated cotton data with a production decision-making model, introduced plant-protection robots, and applied Internet of Things to deliver water and fertilizer. As a result, fertilizer use efficiency rose by 20 to 30 percent, while water consumption dropped by more than 30 percent. Li Guozhao, a veteran cotton farmer, recalled that 36 years ago, he planted 15 mu of cotton. At that time, he cut cotton stalks by hand, irrigated the land by flooding, topped plants manually and hired pickers. By season's end, his hands were often covered with blood blisters. Today, his 350 mu of cotton requires only two hired workers. Drone-based plant protection and machine picking cost as low as 160 yuan (about 23.83 U.S. dollars) to 180 yuan per mu. His next step is to install smart valves for irrigation, so he can water the fields via a tap on his phone. The United States' so-called "Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act" took effect in 2022, and has since disrupted Xinjiang cotton exports to the U.S. market. "But the U.S. sanctions have had no impact on me," Li said. In Xinjiang, the traditional hoe known locally as a khetman has long been replaced by Beidou satellite navigation, just as hand-picking cotton has made way for machine harvesting, leaving no ground for the "forced labor" narrative. Across Xinjiang, a "super cotton field" project featuring extremely high unmanned operation rates in management had been extended to over 2 million mu by the end of 2025. At present, the comprehensive mechanization rate for cotton cultivation and harvesting in Xinjiang has reached 97 percent, with machine-picking accounting for over 90 percent. FULL-INDUSTRIAL-CHAIN STRENGTH Resilience does not only grow in the fields. It extends into factory workshops. Xinjiang is promoting local processing of the entire chain from planting, ginning and spinning to weaving, dyeing and garment-making. In 2025, the share of cotton processed locally reached 45 percent. During the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026-2030), the region plans to continue developing industries of high-count combed yarn, home textiles and technical textiles. In southern Xinjiang, Aksu and Bayingolin have laid out million-spindle intelligent spinning bases, while Kashgar and Hotan are taking on apparel and home-textile manufacturing. Dyeing and finishing operations are being concentrated in industrial parks for low-carbon upgrades. In digital factories, intelligent cotton blending, automated transfer and real-time management systems are already online. On April 10, an express train loaded with 1,118 tonnes of cotton departed from Bachu Station in Xinjiang for Zibo in east China's Shandong Province, which is 4,600 kilometers away. The entire lifespan of each cotton bale, from field picking and factory processing to rail transport, was recorded by Internet of Things systems. A receiving company can scan a code to see which Xinjiang cotton field the bale came from, which production line it passed through, and what temperature and humidity changes it experienced on the train. Xinjiang, as China's "cotton granary," has continued to improve cotton output and quality in recent years and consolidate its advantage in large-scale farming, said Liang Yong, a national political advisor and director of the Xinjiang cotton industry development leading group office. At the 2026 Xinjiang Cotton and Yarn Industry Development Forum held on Sept. 9, Liang noted that the region's textile and apparel industry has risen markedly in the national industrial landscape, with segments such as yarn, grey fabric and chemical fiber accelerating into the front ranks. Originally aimed at blocking Xinjiang cotton from the U.S. market, sanctions have instead sped up the creation of a self-sufficient green manufacturing system. Sustainable cotton standards, low-carbon accounting and better quality for better prices are gradually taking hold. As experts at the forum noted, the more integrated the industrial chain becomes, the weaker the impact from any single-point blockade. False narratives can be repeated and sanctions can be escalated, but truth will prevail, as the thriving cotton industry in Xinjiang attests. Here, season after season of high yields have shown that what sanctions cannot touch is an agricultural system successfully integrating technology, land, people and the industrial chain. Earlier this week, the U.S. Department of Homeland Security announced that it had added three Chinese entities to the so-called "Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act Entity List," which China strongly condemns and firmly opposes.

https://www.chinadaily.com.cn/a/202610/3.body: China discovers huge zircon sand deposit in Xinjiang - Chinadaily.com.cn Search HOME CHINA WORLD BUSINESS CULTURE TRAVEL VIDEO SPORTS OPINION REGIONAL NEWSPAPER MOBILE Global Edition ASIA 中文 双语 Français HOME CHINA WORLD BUSINESS CULTURE TRAVEL VIDEO SPORTS OPINION REGIONAL NEWSPAPER China Daily PDF China Daily E-paper MOBILE China News Society Innovation HK/Macao Cross-Strait Cover Story Photo Environment Health Military Video Home / China / Society Home China Society China discovers huge zircon sand deposit in Xinjiang By Li Menghan | chinadaily.com.cn | Updated: 2026-10-31 16:25 Share Share - WeChat CLOSE China has discovered a major zircon sand deposit in Baicheng county, Aksu prefecture, Xinjiang Uygur autonomous region, with a confirmed resource scale equivalent to more than 40 large zircon deposits, and associated hafnium at a super-large scale, the Ministry of Natural Resources said on Saturday. Zirconium is a silvery-gray transition metal with a high melting point, corrosion resistance and a small neutron absorption cross-section, making it a critical material for nuclear reactor fuel rod cladding and aerospace high-temperature alloys. Hafnium, often found alongside zirconium, boasts a high density and melting point. It is a key material for nuclear reactor control rods and is also used in rocket engines and spacecraft heat shields. The global distribution of zircon resources is uneven, with around 70 percent of reserves concentrated in Australia, while China holds less than 1 percent. This discovery fills a national gap in the quest for super-large zircon deposits and will significantly enhance China's resource security for this mineral. Zhu Yilin, chief engineer of Xinjiang's natural resources department, said at a news conference in Beijing that the discovery is the result of a two-decade sustained exploration effort. Between 2006 and 2019, geologists reanalyzed legacy geochemical survey data from the Tianshan region and identified multiple zircon anomalies and prospective targets. Since 2024, the regional government has allocated 35.19 million yuan ($5.28 million) for five zircon exploration projects, achieving this significant breakthrough after intensive fieldwork, Zhu said. The deposit was named Yuhai in recognition of the contributions made by geologists Peng Yu and Wang Haitao in the discovery. https://24.kg/en/article/aigul-japarova-.body: Kyrgyzstan’s First Lady Aigul Japarova urged society not to turn a blind eye to domestic violence and to provide timely assistance to women and children affected by abuse. She made the statement on October 30 at the first meeting of the High Honorary Council on Family and Women’s Issues of the Organization of Turkic States in Ankara. In her address, Japarova stressed that public silence surrounding cases of domestic violence remains one of the serious problems. She said it is essential to listen to every woman and girl affected by abuse, ensure they have access to legal, psychological and social support, and strengthen cooperation between government agencies and civil society organizations. "Let us work together to build a society where every woman feels safe in her own home and every child grows up surrounded by love and care,” the First Lady said. Japarova also addressed women’s participation in political and public life. She noted that Kyrgyzstan’s legislation provides for women to hold at least 30 percent of seats in the Zhogorku Kenesh, the country’s parliament. The First Lady emphasized that family responsibilities should not prevent women from pursuing education, professional development and self-fulfillment. Speaking about government support for families, she mentioned the monthly Bala Yrysy allowance for children under the age of three and My Home (Menin Uyum) housing program. Another topic of her address was children’s online safety. Aigul Japarova highlighted the risks posed by harmful content and the need to protect minors’ personal data. She noted that Kyrgyzstan’s Digital Code establishes specific requirements for protecting children’s personal data. At the same time, the First Lady urged parents to maintain trusting relationships with their children and pay attention to their online activities. Concluding her address, Japarova underscored the importance of cooperation among Turkic states in protecting women, supporting families and raising children.

Yesterday, 20:30 1 min read 50 views 0 comments 0 Source: Senate of the Oliy Majlis Uzbekistan's parliamentary delegation, led by Tanzila Narbayeva, Chairperson of the Senate of the Oliy Majlis, participated in the 4th Inter-Parliamentary Forum of Central Asian States, held in Dushanbe, Tajikistan. The forum, organized under the theme "Solidarity for Peace, Security, and Prosperity in Central Asia," brought together heads of parliaments and delegations from countries across the region. During the event, Narbayeva presented proposals aimed at strengthening peace and stability in Central Asia, developing mutual trust and good-neighborly relations, expanding trade and economic cooperation, and ensuring the rational use of water and energy resources. In her speech, Narbayeva put forward proposals covering regional peace and stability, trade and economic relations, water and energy resource management, and inter-parliamentary cooperation. The importance of the political will of Central Asian heads of state in strengthening mutual trust and good-neighborly relations was emphasized. Particular attention was given to the role of parliaments in ensuring the consistent implementation of agreements reached between countries. The discussions also addressed strengthening cooperation to counter threats to common security and exchanging legislative experience. Other areas of focus included expanding legislative cooperation, strengthening parliamentary oversight and developing closer ties between local representative bodies. The organization of joint parliamentary discussions on common regional issues was also highlighted. At the conclusion of the forum, participants exchanged views on strengthening peace and stability in Central Asia and developing mutual trust and good-neighborly relations. https://daryo.uz/en/2026/10/29/uzbekista.body: Uzbekistan Uzbekistan ranks among top five countries in poverty reduction, deputy minister says Uzbekistan’s poverty rate fell from 5.8% to 3.6% in the first 10 months of 2026, reducing the number of people classified as poor from 2.2mn to 1.4mn, while the country accounted for 60% of poverty reduction across Central Asia, First Deputy Minister of Employment Marat Jurayev announced, citing findings attributed to World Bank experts. Yesterday, 18:18 2 min read 3 139 views 0 comments 0 Source: “Daryo” Uzbekistan ranked among the world’s top five countries for poverty reduction, with the country accounting for 60% of the decline in poverty across Central Asia, First Deputy Minister of Employment Marat Jurayev announced at a press conference in Tashkent on October 28. According to a Daryo correspondent, Jurayev cited findings attributed to World Bank experts, describing Uzbekistan as a global leader in reducing poverty. “ “The World Bank report noted that Uzbekistan is a global champion in poverty reduction, that is, it is among the top five countries. At the same time, it was stated that 60% of poverty reduction within the Central Asian region falls on Uzbekistan,” the deputy minister said. According to Jurayev, Uzbekistan’s poverty rate fell from 5.8% at the beginning of 2026 to 3.6% by October, reducing the number of people classified as poor from 2.2mn to 1.4mn. It was reported that the number of poor households also declined over the first nine months of the year, from 533,000 to 349,000. Ministry figures show that 824,000 people secured permanent jobs between January and September 2026. During the same period, nearly 4.14mn people received assistance to increase their incomes, while the employment status of 980,000 people working informally was formalized. The figures indicate a continued decline in poverty and an expansion of formal employment, although the ministry did not provide further details on the methodology used to calculate the poverty rate or the World Bank report cited by the deputy minister. Earlier, Daryo reported that Uzbekistan’s poverty rate had fallen from 5.8% to 3.9% in the first eight months of 2026. During this period, more than 160,000 people were employed, 304,000 were involved in entrepreneurship and 22,000 received vocational training. The government also allocated UZS 700bn ($58.4mn) in loans and UZS 77bn ($6.4mn) in loans and subsidies to support low-income families. For 2026, the government set a target of lifting 1.1mn people, or 263,000 families, out of poverty. # Economic Development Policy # Ministry of Employment # Social Welfare Programs # World Bank Assessment # poverty reduction # uzbekistan Muharrir Moxinur Sultanova All stories Telegram channel @daryo_eng Subscribe What do you think? https://www.azernews.az/region/266525.ht.body: Russia's Novaya Gazeta announces closure after 33 years, citing state pressure 30 October 2026 16:45 (UTC+04:00) Akbar Novruz Read more Russia's independent newspaper Novaya Gazeta has announced that it will cease operations on November 9, ending more than three decades of journalism amid what its editorial staff describes as sustained pressure from Russian authorities and security services. In a statement titled "They Killed Us," published on October 30, the newspaper said it would vacate its Moscow editorial offices, where it had operated for nearly 30 years, and shut down its servers. "On November 9, we will turn off the lights of the house we have lived in for 30 years, shut down the servers, and leave. The newspaper is no more. The Russian authorities and special services have forced the editorial office to cease operations," the statement said. The publication attributed its closure to years of censorship, criminal proceedings against journalists, financial restrictions and pressure on its editorial operations. According to the newspaper, its reader donation system was disabled around the same time it received notice to vacate its premises, depriving the publication of a major source of funding. The editorial staff described these developments as part of a coordinated campaign aimed at forcing the newspaper to shut down. Years of pressure on independent journalism Novaya Gazeta said restrictions against the publication intensified following Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022. Its online resources were blocked, its printing equipment was seized and its media registration was revoked later that year. Several journalists subsequently left Russia. The newspaper also recalled attacks and legal proceedings targeting its staff, including an assault on co-founder and 2021 Nobel Peace Prize laureate Dmitry Muratov. It cited the abduction and severe beating of investigative journalist Yelena Milashina in Chechnya, as well as the arrest of editor Oleg Roldugin and searches involving editor-in-chief Sergey Sokolov. In September 2026, Russia's Ministry of Justice designated Novaya Gazeta a "foreign agent," a classification the newspaper said also affected more than 100 journalists and contributors. The editorial staff argued that these measures reflected broader restrictions on freedom of expression and civil rights in Russia. Three decades of investigative reporting Founded in 1993, Novaya Gazeta established itself as one of Russia's most prominent independent newspapers, publishing investigations into government corruption, human rights violations and the wars in Chechnya. Its journalists frequently reported on politically sensitive subjects, including allegations of abuses by security agencies and regional authorities. Several members of its editorial team were murdered over the years. Among them was investigative journalist Anna Politkovskaya, internationally recognised for her reporting on human rights abuses in Chechnya. She was shot dead in her Moscow apartment building in October 2006. In 2021, Dmitry Muratov, then the newspaper's editor-in-chief, received the Nobel Peace Prize for his efforts to safeguard freedom of expression. The newspaper said it would publish a final issue before closing. Concluding its October 30 statement, the editorial staff reflected on the subjects it had covered throughout its existence. "That's what we wrote about all these years. As much as we could. That's why they killed us." Tags: Russia Russian investigative journalist Novaya Gazeta

https://24.kg/en/article/kyrgyzstans-tra.body: The number of deputy heads at Kyrgyzstan's Ministry of Transport and Communications has been increased from three to four. The relevant resolution was signed by Chairman of the Cabinet of Ministers Adylbek Kasymaliev. The amendments have been made to Resolution No. 264 of November 15, 2021, which regulates the maximum staffing levels of government agencies. Under the document, Appendix No. 5, which specifies the number of deputy heads of government agencies, has been amended to increase the figure for the Ministry of Transport from three to four. The decision was made in implementation of Presidential Order No. 329 of September 17, 2026, signed by President Sadyr Japarov. It is aimed at improving the ministry's operational efficiency. The ministry's overall staff size will remain unchanged. The additional senior management position will be created within the existing approved staffing limits. Funding will also be provided through resources allocated to the Ministry of Transport in the national budget for this year and subsequent years. The resolution does not provide for any additional budget allocations. The document will enter into force in 10 days after its adoption.

https://www.trend.az/casia/kazakhstan/42.body: Home Central Asia Kazakhstan Kazakhstan and Singapore aviation authorities sign cooperation statement Kazakhstan News 31 October 2026 09:54 (UTC +04:00) Photo: Ministry of Transport of Kazakhstan Alyona Pavlenko Journalist, International Desk Read more BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 31. The Aviation Administration of Kazakhstan (AAK) and the Civil Aviation Authority of Singapore (CAAS) have signed a Statement of Intent (SOI) to deepen technical cooperation in civil aviation, support growing connectivity, and facilitate increased passenger and cargo traffic between the two countries and their respective regions, according to the Ministry of Transport of Kazakhstan. During the AAK delegation's visit to Singapore, the statement was signed by AAK Chief Executive Officer Michael Daniel and CAAS Director-General Han Kok Juan. Kazakhstan and Singapore are important aviation hubs in Central Asia and Southeast Asia, respectively, and air connectivity between the two countries has grown significantly in recent years. Under the SOI, the two authorities will seek to establish a forward-looking strategic partnership covering key areas of civil aviation cooperation, including flight safety and aviation security, sustainable aviation development, innovation and emerging technologies, as well as aviation inspector training and workforce development. The SOI significantly expands the scope of cooperation, which was previously limited to the delivery of aviation training programs in Kazakhstan under a Cooperation in Training Agreement signed in 2024. AAK and CAAS will work to formalize the expanded cooperation through a new Memorandum of Understanding (MoU), which is planned to be signed in the first half of 2027 during a visit by CAAS to Kazakhstan. The MoU will provide an institutional framework for high-level technical cooperation in civil aviation between Kazakhstan and Singapore, including an annual meeting co-chaired by the heads of the two authorities. The meetings will alternate between Kazakhstan and Singapore to review progress and identify opportunities for further cooperation. "Strengthening cooperation with CAAS is an important step toward further enhancing the professional capabilities of our aviation specialists. We see significant value in exchanging experience and best practices in risk-based oversight, flight safety and aviation security, as well as inspector training. We look forward to developing our existing partnership with CAAS, expanding specialized training and professional development opportunities, and promoting closer cooperation in support of safe, efficient and sustainable civil aviation in Kazakhstan," AAK Chief Executive Officer Michael Daniel said. In turn, Han Kok Juan noted that signing this Statement of Intent demonstrates the shared commitment of the two civil aviation authorities to deepening technical cooperation, bringing the countries and regions closer together, promoting exchanges between aviation professionals and business representatives, and creating new economic opportunities. "We look forward to establishing a formal framework for annual meetings that will enable our aviation sectors to develop a lasting partnership," he said. Uzbekistan’s President Shavkat Mirziyoyev has thanked the President of Azerbaijan Ilham Aliyev for his contribution to strengthening fraternal ties among the Turkic peoples and developing relations within the framework of the Organization of Turkic States (OTS). https://www.trend.az/azerbaijan/4241247..body: Home Azerbaijan Chronicles of Victory: President Ilham Aliyev interviewed by German ARD TV channel on October 31, 2020 (PHOTO/VIDEO) Azerbaijan News 31 October 2026 07:00 (UTC +04:00) BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 31. The Azerbaijani Army launched a counter-offensive operation, later called the "Iron Fist", on September 27, 2020, in response to the large-scale provocation of the Armenian armed forces along the frontline. The 44-day second Karabakh war ended with the liberation of Azerbaijan’s territories from nearly 30-year Armenian occupation and the restoration of territorial integrity. President of the Republic of Azerbaijan Ilham Aliyev has been interviewed by German ARD TV channel. Trend presents the interview. - On the 27th of September, the war started. What is your answer to the question ‘who shot first?’ - The answer is Armenia and we have evidences, because the first victims among civilians and military personnel were Azerbaijanis. That was a third in a row military provocation against us. The first was in July, when they launched an attack on the state border between Armenia and Azerbaijan. And we had casualties among the civilians and the military personnel. The second attempt was in August when Armenia sent a sabotage group, whose leader was detained and he gave evidence that he was sent in order to attack the civilians. And the third time on the 27th of September they launched a heavy artillery bombardment on some of the villages and cities situated close to the line of contact. We responded. So that’s how it started. - You responded tough and harsh. Why like this, this time? Is it a pre-dominance of the Azerbaijan military, because of the drones from Israel and Türkiye? - We had these drones from Israel already for many years and by the way, some of them were used in 2016 during Armenian another provocation which launched in the liberation of the part of the occupied territories. But that clash lasted for several days because Armenia stopped. And if they stopped this time, we would have stopped also. But they did not. They wanted to make a big damage. They started to shell the cities which situated far beyond the line of contact. And we had many victims among civilians so far- 69. So we had to defend ourselves, defend our people and to respond. So our response was harsh, but they deserved it. - As far as I understand, you gained some grounds in the south especially, but as well, I mean next to Karabakh, further in the north and how long will this war continue? - It depends on Armenia, I said many times. We are ready to stop today. And by the way, the fact that three times we agreed for ceasefire demonstrates our will to stop military confrontation and to resolve this issue on the negotiation table by political purposes, political means. But 3 times Armenia brutally violated the ceasefire. - But they say the same. - But look yes, definitely they do. But look at what happened. On the 10th of October, the humanitarian ceasefire was announced. The next day they launched a ballistic missile attack on Ganja from the territory of Armenia. Probably you have seen the devastation which it caused. Ten people were killed, civilians. They said it was not them. But it is clear, because the launch of the ballistic missiles is observed by the satellite. So, the three co-chair countries of the Minsk Group definitely know who did it. The second time they did the same, they violated the ceasefire two minutes after it was announced. And the third time yesterday when they launched a cluster bomb on the city of Tartar. Four people were killed among them one seven year old girl. So it was them. There was no evidence that we did it. What we do is opposite. I said that we will not respond them the same way. We will respond them on the battlefield. We do not attack cities, we do not attack civilians, only on the battlefield. But we have to defend ourselves. If they attack, if they want to regain the positions which they lost, we cannot just stay calm. We need to defend and the more we defend the more territories we liberate. - But exactly the same thing they claimed as well. They say that you use cluster bombs and I mean there was even like some proves from Amnesty International and Human Rights Watch that you used cluster bombs there in Karabakh. I mean, why do you use this kind of arms? - We don’t use. We defend ourselves. We invited Amnesty International and Human Rights Watch to come to Azerbaijan. Unfortunately, their coverage of the events is only from Armenian side. They did not approach us to come here, therefore, we have big doubts about their impartiality. - But now they come. As far as I understand, Human Rights Watch, they are coming or they told me. - They are coming, because we said "why don’t you come here?" After we made a request to them. "Please, do come here", they agreed to come. But why didn’t they come in the first place? - They told me that they wanted to come. They asked for several times, but you didn’t give them access. - No, no. That is not possible. Because that was what we did. Just yesterday we said, why they don’t come, let them come and go to Ganja, go to Tartar, meet the people whom Armenians attacked. And again, the ballistic missile launch is seen from the satellite. No one can say that we launched a ballistic missile on any civilian compound in Nagorno-Karabakh or in Armenia. - Let me ask you again about this cluster munition. Because, of course, you know it’s very serious subject. I had a look into the research of Human Rights Watch and the proof was quite interesting, they had pictures, and they even have names. The name of the weapon they said LAR 160 cluster bomb from Israel. Do you really want to dispute that fact? - Yes, of course. There are no proofs about that. And I would like them to come here, and to give these proofs. At the same time, to go to Ganja, to go to Tartar, to go to Barda and see what kind of weapons Armenians are using. And be impartial... - So, if they can find weapons here, you rely on their research. - No, they will have to, because there is no way for them to say "no". Let them say, because so far, Human Rights Watch and Amnesty International was very aggressive against Azerbaijan. They never made any comment about violation of human rights in Armenia. When a journalist died in Armenian prison they were silent. When leader of main opposition party of Armenia was jailed, they were silent. When former presidents are on trial, they were silent. They don’t want to see it, because they have the so-called Armenian origin people in their structures. And these organizations are basically used in order to damage the image of Azerbaijan. But nevertheless, we invited them. Let them come. And say what they see. - Actually, you never signed the UN Convention on cluster munition. So, why is it a problem for you? Actually you could use it. - But did Armenia sign? - We are talking about Azerbaijan and not Armenia. - We are talking about the conflict. We are talking about the conflict and the fact that we sign or don’t sign any kind of convention doesn’t mean that we are using it or not. We have enough ammunition. We have modern weapons and we demonstrate it on the battlefield. And what we do, we liberate the territories not with bombs. We liberate the territories with our fighters which take one village after another, one city after another, raise the Azerbaijani flag. So, that’s how it is done. - Coming to this subject, I mean, wouldn’t it be a goal somehow to take over those seven districts and afterwards to negotiate and maybe to come into autonomous zone of Karabakh? - We suggested that but Armenians always rejected. The co-chairs of the Minsk Group can prove what I say. We always suggested, we always were committed to the peace plan, so-called basic principles which provided the liberation of the occupied territories of Azerbaijan in phases. https://kloop.kg/blog/2026/10/29/rozysk-.body: Facebook Twitter VK Telegram WhatsApp Журналисты «Клоопа» выяснили, что с 2020 года Курманбека Бакиева и его сыновей исключили из российского реестра розыска*. По какой причине это произошло — неизвестно. Под фамилиями Салиевых и Бакаевых, которые они использовали после побега из Кыргызстана, в базе их тоже нет. В числе разыскиваемых в этой базе есть только Адилбек Салиевич Бакиев** — брат Курманбека. Свергнутый президент Курманбек Бакиев и члены его семьи заочно приговорены в Кыргызстане к долговременным тюремным срокам, вплоть до пожизненного заключения. После революции 2010 года они сбежали из Кыргызстана и власти страны несколько раз заявляли, что безуспешно пытались их экстрадировать . Когда конкретно в 2020 году Бакиевых перестали разыскивать в России — неизвестно. Однако еще в июне 2020 года Генеральная прокуратура Кыргызстана заявляла , что ведет работу по «реализации принудительных мер по возвращению в страну» Бакиевых. В октябре 2020 года в результате митингов против результатов парламентских выборов к власти пришел бывший соратник Бакиевых — нынешний президент Садыр Жапаров. В базе международного розыска «Интерпола» Бакиевых тоже нет***. Призывы простить Бакиева и обещание помилования Во время правления Бакиевых, Жапаров занимал разные позиции на государственных постах — от советника президента до главы Нацагентства по предотвращению коррупции. За шесть лет его правления в кыргызских соцсетях неоднократно обсуждали вопрос того, что он пытается реабилитировать Бакиевых. И тому было множество оснований, начиная от заявлений Жапарова, заканчивая решением Конституционного суда. Жапаров говорил об этом еще будучи и.о. президента в декабре 2020 года на выступлении перед избирателями в Гулчо, в Алайском районе Ошской области. Тогда он заявил, что вернет в Кыргызстан беглых президентов Аскара Акаева и Курманбека Бакиева, если их «народ простит». «Если много людей попросит, если народ простит обоих, тогда привезем. Если большинство будет против — трудно будет», — сказал Жапаров. После того, как Жапаров уже стал президентом, в апреле 2021 года тогдашний генпрокурор Курманкул Зулушев утверждал , что над экстрадицией Бакиевых работают. Хотя, как выяснили журналисты, в российской базе розыска Бакиевых уже не было. Спустя год Зулушев сказал , что экстрадировать Бакиевых «нет возможности». В феврале 2023 года президент Садыр Жапаров встречался с Бакиевым и другими бывшими кыргызскими президентами в Дубае. Тогда он обратился к кыргызстанцам с просьбой быть милосерднее и «отложить прошлые обиды и жалобы», а после — «объединиться во благо страны». «У предков есть понятие: “Выдай замуж свою мать за того, кто убил твоего отца” (“атаңды өлтургөнгө энеңди алып бер”). Если по исламу, то мы увидим, что уметь прощать — обычай. [...] Если мы хотим укрепить свой суверенитет, независимость и развивать наш Кыргызстан, давайте отложим в сторону все прошлое, обиды и жалобы», — сказал он. Однако некоторые политики увидели в этой встрече попытку реабилитации Курманбека Бакиева. Один из них — бывший президент Алмазбек Атамбаев. Тогда он заявил , что установление мира и единства в стране и возвращение Бакиевых в Кыргызстан — разные вещи, совмещение которых «даст иной результат». Через несколько месяцев после встречи в Дубае, Жапаров сказал, что если Курманбек Бакиев вернется в Кыргызстан, то его задержат, но он может рассмотреть вопрос о его помиловании. «Я не имею права отменять решения суда. У меня только есть право помиловать или отказать, если Курманбек Бакиев попросит об этом. Решение помиловать или нет я буду принимать, учитывая мнение пострадавших в 2010 году», — сказал Жапаров в интервью госагенству «Кабар» в мае 2023. В начале 2025 появлялись слухи о приезде в Кыргызстан Максима Бакиева, Жаныша Бакиева и других членов клана. А позже, в апреле 2025, Конституционный суд Кыргызстана разрешил пересмотр уголовных дел в отношении Курманбека Бакиева при его личном участии. Суд объяснил решение тем, что приговор ему выносили заочно — свергнутый президент Бакиев и его родственники успели покинуть страну до начала уголовного преследования. * Всех разыскиваемых в России людей можно проверить в базе, доступной на сайте издания «Медиазона» , которое публикует их в удобном формате и ежедневно обновляет информацию. Например, в ней уже можно найти членов движения «Шумкар», которых кыргызские власти признали экстремистскими в начале октября: политаналитика Айдара Раева, эколога Самата Кушбека, бывшего назначенца Садыра Жапарова Тенгиза Болтурука и политблогера Сыргака Кенжебаева. ** Адилбека Бакиева в России разыскивают с 28 июля 2020 года. За что его разыскивают — неизвестно, но в розыск подал Кыргызстан. По информации на 2019 год известно , что он проживал в Казахстане. В июне 2020 года Генпрокуратура Кыргызстана сообщала , что Адилбек Бакиев находится в числе других членов семьи, в отношении которых заочно были вынесены приговоры. Тогда надзорный орган говорил , что «идет работа по реализации принудительных мер по возвращению в страну Курманбека Бакиева, его братьев Жаныбека, Адилбека, Марата, Каныбека, его сына Максима и других». Было это за несколько месяцев до прихода к власти Садыра Жапарова. В 2023, уже после того как Жапаров занял президентский пост, он утверждал , что свергнутого президента Бакиева и ближайших членов его семьи разыскивают, а против Адилбека, по его данным, нет даже уголовных дел. *** В 2010 году «Интерпол» объявил в розыск Максима Бакиева, но сейчас он в списках не числится. В январе 2016 «Интерпол» отказался вносить в свою базу Курманбека Бакиева, его брата Каныбека и старшего сына Марата. Заместитель начальника Национального центрального бюро Интерпола Даирбек Казыбаев на пресс-конференции в январе 2016 заявлял , что Бакиевых ищут по линии межгосударственного розыска. Но числятся ли они до сих пор в межгосударственном или национальном розыске — неизвестно. Публичных реестров этих розысков нет в открытом доступе, поэтому это невозможно проверить. ЭТО МОЖЕТ БЫТЬ ИНТЕРЕСНО ЕЩЕ ОТ АВТОРА Садыр Жапаров: Максим Бакиев — жмот, не дал денег ни друзьям, ни отцу Садыр Жапаров признал, что Алексей Ширшов стоит за майнингом на Камбар-Ате 2. «Клооп» писал об этом еще три года назад Ширшов и 7 млрд сомов на благоустройство Каракола. За чей счет банкет?

https://bih.osce.org/news/mission-bosnia.body: News News Item Building a Shared Future: National Minorities at the Heart of Reconciliation in BiH Issued on: 29 October 2026 Issued by: OSCE Mission to Bosnia and Herzegovina Fields of work: Human rights , National minority issues , Roma and Sinti , Rule of law Sarajevo, 29 October 2026 – Genuine reconciliation and lasting peace in Bosnia and Herzegovina cannot be achieved without the equal participation of all citizens, including national minorities whose perspectives have too often been excluded from political and public dialogue. This was the central message of the conference “Beyond the ‘Others’ – Inclusive Reconciliation and the Future of Bosnia and Herzegovina” , held today in Sarajevo. Organized by the Jewish Cultural, Educational and Humanitarian Society La Benevolencija, Kali Sara – Roma Information Centre and Olam Aid, with the support of the OSCE Mission to Bosnia and Herzegovina, the event brought together representatives of Jewish and Roma communities, institutions, civil society, academia and international organizations. Discussions focused on the importance of including national minorities in transitional justice, dealing with the past and reconciliation processes. Participants addressed persistent barriers to political and institutional equality, the recognition of different communities’ historical experiences, and the role of young people in strengthening mutual trust, social cohesion and respect for diversity. The participants concluded that Bosnia and Herzegovina cannot be a truly democratic society as long as the rights of certain citizens remain restricted on the basis of their ethnic affiliation or identity. Reconciliation requires confronting the past, acknowledging historical facts, ensuring justice, and building mutual trust. Jews, Roma and other national minorities must be equal participants in shaping the future of BiH, while educating younger generations is essential to overcoming prejudice and divisions. The ultimate goal is not merely to secure greater rights and opportunities for “Others”, but to build a Bosnia and Herzegovina where no one is treated as a second-class citizen, diversity is valued rather than seen as an obstacle, and equality is a lived reality rather than merely a principle enshrined in law. The conference also highlighted the importance of cultural heritage in bringing communities together. An evening cultural programme, “Melodies of Coexistence: A Sephardic and Romani Cultural Evening” , celebrated the shared cultural heritage and traditions of Jewish and Roma communities, reinforcing the message that an inclusive future for Bosnia and Herzegovina must be built on equality, mutual understanding and respect for all its citizens.

https://uzbekistan.osce.org/news/project.body: News News Item OSCE-supported seminar in Tashkent discusses establishing Aarhus Centres in Uzbekistan Issued on: 29 October 2026 Issued by: OSCE Project Co-ordinator in Uzbekistan The prospects for establishing Aarhus Centres in Uzbekistan were the focus of a seminar on 26 October in Tashkent, organized by the OSCE Project Co-ordinator in Uzbekistan, the State Environmental Expertise Center and the Central Asian Green University. The event brought together 40 participants. They included representatives of state bodies, civil society organizations, academia, and students of the University. Participants learned about the Aarhus Convention’s three pillars: access to environmental information, public participation in decision-making, and access to justice. They also heard about the experience of OSCE-supported Aarhus Centres in other Central Asian countries. A panel discussion brought together state, civil society, academic and youth perspectives on the possible organizational models, functions and partnerships of future Aarhus Centres in Uzbekistan. Participants heard about the experience of OSCE-supported Aarhus Centres in other Central Asian countries Gayrat Mukhamedov, Director of the State Environmental Expertise Center, said open environmental information and active public participation were key conditions for effective environmental governance. He added that Aarhus Centres would strengthen dialogue between the state and society. The OSCE Project Co-ordinator in Uzbekistan continues to support Uzbekistan in implementing the Aarhus Convention and promoting the involvement of women and youth in environmental decision-making. https://ashgabat.osce.org/news/centre-as.body: News News Item OSCE promotes exchange of best practices between national human rights institutions of Moldova and Turkmenistan Issued on: 29 October 2026 Issued by: OSCE Centre in Ashgabat Fields of work: Human rights Representatives of the Office of the Ombudsperson of Turkmenistan and the Office of the People’s Advocate (Ombudsperson) of the Republic of Moldova exchanged practical experiences during an OSCE-organized peer-to-peer seminar held in Ashgabat on 28 and 29 October 2026. The two-day event focused on the mandates and functions of ombudsperson institutions, human rights protection and the handling of individual complaints. Ceslav Panico, People’s Advocate of the Republic of Moldova, provided an overview of the status and mandate of his office, elaborating on its legal status and the guarantees of its independence and inviolability. Representatives of the two institutions discussed the general and specific functions of their respective offices, as well as their co-operation with other national and international institutions. “Independent national human rights institutions play an important role in ensuring respect for human rights, addressing citizens’ complaints and helping to improve national protection mechanisms,” said William Leaf, Head of the OSCE Centre in Ashgabat, addressing the seminar participants. Vasile Coroi, People’s Advocate for Children’s Rights (Children’s Ombudsperson) of the Republic of Moldova, shared insights into international and regional frameworks for the protection of children’s rights and presented the mandate and main intervention tools of Moldova’s Ombudsperson for Children’s Rights. Discussions centred on monitoring respect for children’s rights, as well as awareness-raising and information activities. The seminar also covered investigative techniques for handling individual cases, effective fact-finding methodologies and practical interviewing skills for working with victims and witnesses, as well as methods for collecting, preserving and analysing evidence. A dedicated session focused on international and national mechanisms for the protection of women’s rights. https://dushanbe.osce.org/news/programme.body: News News Item OSCE trains border officers from Kyrgyzstan and Tajikistan to verify security documents The OSCE Programme Office in Dushanbe held a learning course on verifying the authenticity of security documents from 19 to 23 October 2026, in Guliston, Sughd Region. Fourteen border officers, seven from the Border Service of Kyrgyzstan and seven from the Border Troops of Tajikistan, participated in the course. Issued on: 30 October 2026 Issued by: OSCE Programme Office in Dushanbe Fields of work: Border management The OSCE Programme Office in Dushanbe held a learning course on verifying the authenticity of security documents from 19 to 23 October 2026 in Guliston, Sughd Region. Fourteen border officers, seven from the Border Service of Kyrgyzstan and seven from the Border Troops of Tajikistan, participated in the course. The officers serve at neighbouring border crossing points along the Tajik-Kyrgyz border. Delivered by four international experts in document security, the course helped participants strengthen their skills in document authentication, security feature design and verification techniques. It covered graphic and printing security features, document personalization methods and the security features of polycarbonate data pages. Practical sessions focused on identifying forged and counterfeit travel documents, including imitated paper security features, altered personal data, photo substitutions and facial morphing. Border officers from Kyrgyzstan and Tajikistan pose for a group photo with international experts at the end of an OSCE learning course on verifying the authenticity of security documents, Guliston, Sughd Region, 23 October 2026. The learning course forms part of the OSCE’s efforts to strengthen border security and cross-border co-operation in Central Asia. By involving officers from both countries, it promoted a shared understanding of document fraud and strengthened professional contacts between border services. The knowledge and skills acquired will help officers identify falsified documents at border crossing points, contributing to more secure border management and the prevention of transnational crime. https://www.rferl.org/a/ukraine-russia-o.body: News US-Brokered Humanitarian Mission In Russian-Occupied Oleshky Under Way, Kyiv And Moscow Say By RFE/RL's Ukrainian Service October 30, 2026 07:30 CET Updated October 30, 2026 12:37 CET US-Brokered Humanitarian Mission In Russian-Occupied Oleshky Under Way, Kyiv And Moscow Say Share Copy link Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Email Share Share Copy link Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Email Share Prefer us on Google Ukraine's human rights ombudsman, Dmytro Lubinets, arrives in Oleshky. A US-brokered mission to allow humanitarian aid into the war-torn Russian-occupied southern Ukrainian city of Oleshky and enable residents to leave safely has begun, Kyiv and Moscow announced. Ukraine's human rights ombudsman, Dmytro Lubinets, and his Russian counterpart, Yana Lantratova, said on October 30 that Ukrainian and Russian delegations had arrived in Oleshky and that people wishing to leave the city were being prepared to be evacuated. "I am currently speaking with local residents to hear their concerns and understand what assistance they need most," Lubinets wrote on Telegram, sharing videos of conversations with local Ukrainians who appeared to cheer the long-awaited support and evacuations. SEE ALSO: White House Says Melania Trump Brokers Localized Cease-Fire For Occupied Ukrainian City Hundreds of Oleshky residents were expected to return to Ukrainian-controlled territory via a roundabout route through Russian-occupied Crimea to Anapa, in southern Russia, and then by plane to the Belarusian city of Homel -- and then by bus into Ukraine's northern Chernihiv region. Map: Evacuating Oleshky Lubinets and Lantratova have previously announced that all Oleshky residents who want to leave the city will be able to do so until 2 p.m. local time, while aid distribution is expected to begin shortly afterwards. They said that designated evacuation routes out of the mine-surrounded city had been cleared, while Lantratova said that "tens of tons of humanitarian aid" were being sent there. For three consecutive days, starting on October 27, Ukraine and Russia observed a localized cease-fire in Oleshky with no violations reported. The arrangement was brokered by US first lady Melania Trump, who announced the agreement a week earlier. Melania Trump said that civilians from both countries were expected to visit people in their homes to assess their needs, while those seeking to evacuate would receive coordinated assistance and transportation to their preferred destinations. "I anticipate some will want to go to Russia, and some to Ukraine," she said. Embed share 'Get Killed Or Starve': Life Under Russian Occupation In Oleshky by RFE/RL Embed share The code has been copied to your clipboard. width px height px The URL has been copied to your clipboard No media source currently available 0:00 0:05:18 0:00 Having spent years living under Russian occupation, some Oleshky residents expressed concern about the evacuation process, fearing "filtration" while traveling through Russian territory, Ukrainian journalist Maria Semenchenko, who grew up in the city, told RFE/RL's Ukrainian Service on October 29. The residents, she said, were concerned about potential "coercive screenings and interrogations used by Russia to identify people deemed disloyal," adding that "some have already experienced torture in the past" and that she knew "at least one person who does not want to leave for precisely this reason." Russian forces captured Oleshky early in the full-scale invasion of Ukraine that Moscow launched in 2022. Later that year, it effectively became a frontline city after Ukraine retook the regional capital, Kherson, less than 10 kilometers away on the other side of the Dnieper River. Once home to around 24,000 people, Oleshky's population has declined dramatically due to displacement and deaths caused by Russia's war. The destruction of the nearby Kakhovka Dam in June 2023 further compounded the devastation, with an estimated 90 percent of the city's territory flooded. Fewer than 2,000 people remained in the city by the fall, including around 50 children, according to Melania Trump's office. Most are believed to be elderly residents who have been unable or unwilling to leave. Remaining in a largely ruined city that is ringed by land mines, Oleshky residents for months were trapped in a war zone that is cut off from the outside world, with little to no food, drinking water, medicine, or electricity. SEE ALSO: 'We'll Die This Autumn': Ruined And Flooded, Russian-Occupied Oleshky In Ukraine Starves Under A 'Total Blockade' Kyiv has blamed Russia for the dire situation in the city, accusing Moscow of failing to ensure the safety and well-being of civilians. The Kremlin, in turn, has blamed Ukrainian drone strikes for its inability to do so. Ukrainian officials and volunteers had previously told RFE/RL that they believed people in Oleshky were essentially being held hostage to Russia's military goals in the region. While the city has served as an important staging ground for Russian attacks in southern Ukraine, they said its residents were effectively serving as a human shield for Moscow's forces. Its comprehensive coverage also includes award-winning reporting by the Donbas.Realities and Crimea.Realities projects and the Schemes investigative unit. This item is part of News Russia Ukraine

https://serbia.osce.org/news/mission-ser.body: News News Item Cybersecurity co-operation and digital resilience in focus at Cyberfy Summit Issued on: 29 October 2026 Issued by: OSCE Mission to Serbia Fields of work: Cyber/ICT Security The OSCE Mission to Serbia, in partnership with Cyberfy , one of Serbia’s leading regional cybersecurity initiative, supported the organization of the Cyber Security Summit in Belgrade bringing together cybersecurity professionals, decision-makers, representatives of businesses and academia, and innovators from across the region to discuss emerging cyber threats and ways to strengthen digital resilience, on 29 October in Belgrade. Held under the theme “Resilience Without Borders”, the summit addressed key cybersecurity challenges, including the protection of critical infrastructure, the implications of artificial intelligence for cybersecurity, evolving regulatory requirements and the development of operational capacities. “Cyber threats do not recognize institutional boundaries, and our response should not either. Strong public-private co-operation and effective information-sharing are therefore essential,” said the Head of the OSCE Mission to Serbia, Ambassador Marcel Peško. The event provided a platform for exchanging expertise and good practices, while fostering strong co-operation among public institutions, the private sector and other stakeholders working to address cybersecurity challenges across the region. “The OSCE Mission to Serbia remains committed to supporting Serbia’s efforts in this area and to working with our partners towards a more resilient, secure and co-operative digital environment,” Ambassador Peško added. The OSCE Mission to Serbia has been working with national partners to strengthen Serbia’s cybersecurity capacities since 2021. Through its project “Strengthening the Republic of Serbia’s National Capacities on Cybersecurity”, the Mission supports the implementation of Serbia’s National Strategy for the Development of the Information Society and Security 2021-2026. Its activities include institutional capacity-building, international co-operation and initiatives to develop the next generation of cybersecurity professionals. Through its partnership with Cyberfy , the Mission supports dialogue and knowledge exchange among stakeholders, contributing to stronger cybersecurity co-operation and digital resilience in Serbia and the wider region.
